rule: Each timed status passes one ordered pipeline in status_change_start: gates (dead, map, boss/MVP immunity); end-and-return list; fail list checked before any roll; a resistance function that takes a percent term from one stat, then a fixed term, then a chance floor, then one roll; a duration with a percent cut from the same stat, a fixed term applied last that may be negative, and a duration floor. A status that is already active is replaced (timer deleted and restarted, values overwritten) unless its definition says keep-higher. The fail list, not code, decides whether a status blocks itself (Stun) or refreshes (Bleeding). Damage-over-time statuses run on per-status intervals and stop at a fraction of max HP; knockback checks immunity, ends listed statuses and respects roots before moving.

data_fields.name: resistPctPerPoint
data_fields.unit: percent of chance per stat point

data_fields.name: resistFixedBonusPct
data_fields.unit: percent points off chance after percent term

data_fields.name: durationCutPctPerPoint
data_fields.unit: percent of duration per stat point

data_fields.name: failList
data_fields.unit: status ids; a self id blocks re-application

data_fields.name: warnDelayMs
data_fields.unit: ms, warning stage before a delayed status starts

keep: Resist pipeline order: percent resist, fixed resist, floor, one roll, then duration cut, fixed term, floor.
Fail list as the rule for hard-lock chaining (no stacking a lock on a lock).
Refresh-or-block chosen per status in data, not in code.
Stun holds through hits; Freeze breaks on the first hit (RemoveOnDamaged flag).
Stone-wait as a readable warning before the damage phase.
Bleed cannot kill a non-player (damage capped at health minus one).
